categories.name: Claude Code & Codex add-ons
categories.what: Things you bolt onto a coding agent: swarms of sub-agents, workflow packs, slash-command collections. They change how the agent works, not which model it uses.

categories.name: AI gateways & routers
categories.what: One endpoint in front of many models. Swap providers, fall back when one is down or out of quota, track spend. Your tool talks to the gateway; the gateway talks to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others.

categories.name: Token & cost savers
categories.what: Shrink what goes into or comes out of the model (shorter answers, compressed logs) or show you where the money goes. Same work, smaller bill.

categories.name: Coding & personal agents
categories.what: The agent itself: you give it a task, it reads files, runs commands and edits code. Claude Code and Codex are the official ones; these are the alternatives and open-source rivals.

categories.name: Agent frameworks
categories.what: Libraries for developers who want to build their own agent or multi-agent app in code. Not something you install to chat with.

categories.name: Run models locally
categories.what: Download an open-weight model and run it on your own computer or server. Private, free per use, but needs a decent GPU or a lot of RAM.

categories.name: Memory, RAG & knowledge
categories.what: Give AI your documents, codebase or long-term memory. RAG = look up the relevant bits first, then answer. Knowledge graphs store facts and how they connect.

categories.name: No-code builders & chat UIs
categories.what: Build AI workflows by dragging boxes, or run your own ChatGPT-style app for a team. For people who'd rather click than code.
